After more than a decade of never adopting touch screens in its Mac laptop lineup, Apple is finally set to launch its first MacBook with a touch screen as early as October this year, expected to debut alongside the next-generation redesigned MacBook Pro, with the new machine possibly being named the MacBook Ultra.

Of course, rumours are still rumours—but almost all reliable sources agree that the MacBook Pro will support touch functionality later this year. Apple itself has even left a few clues in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh functionality, and slightly larger menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, that last point is particularly annoying for me, because things that used to fit on the left side of the 'notch' are now already starting to spill over.

You could call these coincidences, but it sure looks that way. Regardless, here's what the first MacBook with a touch screen is expected to offer.

OLED Display with Dynamic Island

On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED display, with specs similar to the iPad Pro—the latter often hailed as one of the best mobile displays on the market. Tandem OLED is built by stacking multiple layers of OLED panels, delivering exceptional colour, strong contrast, and higher brightness.

Reports also indicate the new machine will include a Dynamic Island, smaller than the one on iPhone, though it won't support Face ID.

Software Optimisations

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will add several special software optimisations to the first touch-screen MacBook Pro, going beyond what's already seen in the macOS 27 beta:

"For instance, if a user touches a button or interface element, a new type of menu will pop up around the user's finger, offering options better suited for touch interaction. The software will also display the most appropriate combination of controls based on the user's past interaction habits. If a user taps an item on the menu bar at the top of the screen, that set of controls will automatically enlarge to make it easier to operate with a finger."

M5 Pro and M5 Max Chips

Although initial reports indicated the new MacBook Pro would be the first to adopt M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip the release of these two chips and push ahead to the M7. In other words, the first-generation 2nm chips won't appear in this redesigned MacBook Pro; instead, the new machine will use the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

There won't be a base model version of this computer anytime soon, but there are rumours that Apple will launch a base model redesigned MacBook Pro with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly Thinner Body

One of the design rumours about the new MacBook Pro is that the body will be slightly thinner and lighter—but exactly how noticeable this will be remains unclear. The previous generation MacBook Pro already made the machine look and feel quite chunky, so improvements in this area would likely be well received by users—provided thermal performance isn't sacrificed.

Summary

All in all, the first touch-screen MacBook Pro looks like an exciting upgrade. However, because Apple raised prices in June due to a memory shortage, the new machine's pricing will be adjusted accordingly—so I expect the 14-inch model to start at around $2499 and the 16-inch at around $2999.

Are you looking forward to a MacBook with a touch screen? Will you pick one up at launch, or will you wait a while until the base model 14-inch version arrives? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
